answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale.. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. Consider a gale as the anchor of the cost.
